text: Look, a day is coming for the LORD, when your plunder will be divided in your very midst.

I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered, the women violated. Half the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations as he fights on a day of battle.

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two, from east to west, forming a vast valley; half the mountain will move north and half of it south.

You will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley between the mountains will reach to Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew reads "with you," addressing the reader or the city; ancient versions read "with him."

versions.text: You will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley between the mountains will reach to Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew text has the second person ("with you"), while the translation follows the ancient reading "with him." A brief footnote alerts the reader to the textual difference without disturbing the flow.

text:
On that day there will be no light, no cold, no frost.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain; it may also be read: "there will be no light of the shining bodies, but cold and frost."

versions.text: On that day there will be no light—no cold, no frost.
versions.explanation: The dash makes the sentence read as if the absence of light were being defined by the absence of cold, which is confusing when read aloud. A simple list plus a footnote handles the well-known difficulty of the Hebrew.

text: It will be a unique day, known to the LORD alone—neither day nor night—and at evening time there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, in summer and in winter alike.
The LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.

The whole land will be turned into a plain from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will rise high and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
People will live in her, and never again will she be destroyed; Jerusalem will dwell in safety.

This will be the plague with which the LORD strikes all the peoples who wage war against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are still standing on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall upon them. Each will seize the hand of his neighbor, and they will attack one another.
Judah too will fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered in—gold, silver, and clothing in great abundance.
A similar plague will strike the horses and mules, the camels and donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.
Then all who survive of the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
And if any of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, no rain will fall on them.

versions.text: And if any of the families of the earth will not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, no rain will fall on them.
versions.explanation: In an English conditional clause the present tense ("does not go up") is standard; "will not go up" is awkward and slightly ambiguous (suggesting refusal of a wish rather than a condition).

text: If the people of Egypt do not go up and take part, then they too will have no rain, and on them will fall the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.

versions.text: If the people of Egypt do not go up and take part, then they too will have no rain; the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths will fall on them.
versions.explanation: The long subject before the verb ("the plague ... will fall on them") is hard to follow when read aloud; placing the verb first keeps the sentence clear and rhythmic.

text: This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
On that day even the bells on the horses will be inscribed "Holy to the LORD," and the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sacred bowls before the altar.

Every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of hosts, and all who come to sacrifice will take them and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be any trader in the house of the LORD of hosts.
